claims.text: Hf is an oxygen-affinitive element suitable for minor alloy doping.
A TiZrMoW-based refractory HEA can combine high yield strength with substantial impact-induced energy release.
The untreated TiZrMoW-based alloy has limited ductility under dynamic loading.
The untreated TiZrMoW-based alloy is prone to shear localization under dynamic loading.
A small, controlled amount of Hf should be introduced during alloy synthesis.
Minor Hf addition will refine the target alloy's microstructure.
Minor Hf addition will increase the density of deformation twins.
Minor Hf addition will stabilize grain boundaries.
Hf atoms preferentially segregate to dislocation sites and grain boundaries in the target refractory HEA.
Hf segregation facilitates deformation-twin nucleation.
Solute-mediated modification by Hf reduces stress concentrations.
Increased twinning and microstructural refinement delay shear localization under dynamic loading.
A precipitate distribution underpins both high strength and impact-induced energetic release in the target alloy.
Hf doping will maintain the precipitate distribution responsible for strength and energetic release.
Hf doping will increase uniform elongation by approximately 10–20% relative to the untreated alloy.
Hf doping will not reduce yield strength.
Hf doping will not reduce dynamic impact-induced energy release.
The proposed response should apply to refractory HEAs with similar refractory-element matrices and processing histories.
The hypothesis is to be tested under quasi-static loading and dynamic loading near 3000 s^-1.
Higher Hf concentrations might produce deleterious phases.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a ductility increase of at least about 10% while retaining strength and energy release, but the stated rule only falsifies the hypothesis when inadequate ductility improvement is accompanied by a reduction in strength or energy release. Thus, no ductility improvement with unchanged strength and energy would violate the prediction but would not trigger falsification.
